title.text: Budapest City Centre: Real Shooting Experience with 40 Shots and 6 Guns

pills.pop_html: The line-up: Ruger MK IV .22 (10 shots), FÉG P9 "Browning" 9 mm (5), Grand Power P45 .45 ACP (5), Stribog SP9A1 submachine gun (10), M4-style AR carbine in .223 (5) and a Kalashnikov AK-47 in 7.62×39 (5). That works out at €2.16 per shot.

How it runs: An 8-minute safety briefing, about an hour on the lanes, then an optional 15-minute photo stop. The package lists an instructor for every shooter, plus all equipment, ammunition and range fees.
Small extras included: Free coffee and water while you register, and your paper targets to take home. Arrive 15 minutes early for the paperwork.
Rules: Every shooter needs a passport or ID card. Under-18s and pregnant women cannot shoot, and anyone intoxicated is turned away. No licence or experience needed.

best_for.pick_html: for first-timers who want a central indoor range with one instructor per shooter and the classic AK-47 plus M4 combination for €86
best_for.skip_html: if you want the most shots per euro: the Shooting2 packages give 44–60 rounds for €74–90

pills.pop_html: Getting there: An air-conditioned bus collects you from pick-up points in central Budapest and drives you about 20 minutes to the outdoor range and back. Be at the pick-up point 10 minutes before departure.

Choose your package: You pick from pistols, machine guns and assault rifles on arrival. Focus on a single gun or try up to 10 different firearms. €85 is the entry price, and extra guns and ammunition cost more.
What's different: This is the only open-air range on the page, with a 2-hour guided lesson and full kit: eye and ear protection, protective vests and targets. Drinks are included with the session.
Rules: Every shooter must be over 18 and bring a passport or ID card (a copy is accepted). Alcohol and drugs are not allowed.

best_for.pick_html: for groups who want a proper half-day outing at an outdoor range with the transfer sorted, because the bus from the centre is included
best_for.skip_html: if you have an hour between sights: the round trip makes this a 2–3.5 hour commitment

title.text: Budapest: 10-Gun Shooting Experience with Historic Classics

pills.pop_html: The line-up: Handguns: Smith & Wesson 2206 (10 shots), Glock 17 (5), Tokarev TT (5), Colt 1911 Government (5), Rossi R351 revolver (5). Rifles: Hammerli TAC R1 M4 (10), Heckler & Koch SP5 (5), AK-47 (5), Tula SKS (5) and an Oberland Arms OA-16 "Vietnam Retro" (5).
The maths: €89.98 for 60 rounds is €1.50 a shot and €9 a gun. Its two sister packages sit at the same €9 a gun, the lowest per-gun prices on this page.
Group size: Sessions are capped at 6 participants, with instructors explaining each gun before you fire it. Photos with the guns and your target sheet come with the package, plus coffee.
Why this one: It is the only package here that puts a Colt 1911, a Soviet Tokarev TT and a Tula SKS side by side with a Glock and an AK-47, so you feel how designs changed across the 20th century.

best_for.pick_html: for anyone who wants the widest gun line-up per euro, because 10 guns and 60 rounds for €90 is €9 a gun and €1.50 a shot
best_for.skip_html: if you only care about the big rifles: half the rounds here go through pistols

title.text: Budapest: Hollywood Gun Range Shooting Package

pills.pop_html: The line-up: The operator advertises two line-ups of 60 rounds: one with a CZ 512 Tactical (20), AR-9 (15), Scorpion EVO (15), M4 (5) and HS VHS-2 (5), the other with a Ruger P10/22 (20), Scorpion EVO (15), UZI (15), CZ Bren (5) and AK-47 (5). Ask at check-in which set you get.
The maths: €117 (down from €130) for 60 rounds is €1.95 a shot and €23.40 a gun, the same round count as Shooting2's 10-gun package for €27 more.
On the lane: Your range master gives you tips on each gun and feedback on your targets, and you can take pictures to share.
Rules: 18+ only, no licence needed. Not suitable for people under 40 kg, over 80, with epilepsy or heart problems, or pregnant women.

best_for.pick_html: for Churchill fans who want 60 rounds and an UZI or M4 in the mix, because it is the range's biggest standard package
best_for.skip_html: if you are price-sensitive: Shooting2 gives you 60 rounds over 10 guns for €90

The maths: €225 for 55 rounds is €4.09 a shot and €37.50 a gun, almost twice the next-highest price per shot (€2.16 at Capital). You pay for rare WWII and Cold War guns, not volume.
Kalashnikov time: 7 rounds on the AK-47 plus 7 on the short AKSU, the most Kalashnikov time in any package here.
Rules: Alcohol and drugs not allowed. 18+, minimum 140 cm and 40 kg, not suitable for people over 75, with epilepsy or heart problems, or pregnant women.

title.text: Budapest: Indoor Gun Range Shooting Experience

pills.pop_html: Time on the range: A 2-hour guided lesson with a certified instructor, double the hour-long sessions at Churchill. Arrive 10 minutes before your slot.
Choose your package: Pick from pistols, machine guns and assault rifles: one gun or a full selection of up to 10. Eye and ear protection, protective vests and targets are included.
The venue: Four high-capacity lanes at Maglódi út 47 in District X, east of the centre. Drinks are included after shooting.
Rules: Every shooter must be over 18 and bring an ID or passport.

best_for.pick_html: for people who want Ranger's longer 2-hour lesson without the bus trip to the outdoor range
best_for.skip_html: if you are staying central and want to walk: Capital, Shooting2 and Churchill are all in Districts V–VII
